metadata.description: The page manifest of one documentation package in one language (PROP-057 `##SEO-MANIFEST-AND-RESOLVER`, `##DISC-MACHINE-MIRROR`). It is served as `/doc/manifest.json`, it is the source of the site's navigation, and every `llms` tier is derived from it rather than from a second walk of the tree. One manifest is one package, so it is one language: a translation is another package and has a manifest of its own. Nothing here compares versions, fingerprints or revisions (`##OBS-NOTHING-LEAKS`). Source of truth for `crates/vibe-wire/src/generated/doc_manifest/`.
The card and the officiality of the documentation itself — what a shelf, a language selector and a catalogue row show before any page is opened.

Every page of the package, in the reading order the layer law gives them — stable text before text that moves with the product (PROP-048 `##THE-LAYER-LAW`). A package with no pages yet writes `[]`, never an absent key.

Where one documentation stands for one subject (PROP-057 `##REL-OFFICIAL-IS-CONVERGENCE`, `##ROW-DISC-DOCS-STATUS`). `primary` — the subject sent its readers here first; `official` — the subject named it among its own; `community` — only the documentation's own edge is known. Closed by construction: the value is COMPUTED from the convergence of the two edges at every render, and a fourth name would mean a fourth way for edges to meet. It is never stored as a flag in a manifest or an index (`##REL-NO-OFFICIAL-FLAG`); this document is a render, which is exactly why it may carry it.

Where one translation stands for its source documentation (PROP-057 `##LOC-OFFICIAL-TRANSLATION`, `##ROW-DISC-TRANS-STATUS`). `official` — the same group as the source published it under the name `<docname>-<lang>`; everything else is `community`. There is no `primary` on this level: a source documentation sends nobody to one language first.

Which of the two page skeletons a page follows (the package's own `AUTHORING.md` §7, under PROP-057 `##SEO-PAGE-TEMPLATE` and `##MANDATE-PROMPT-FIRST`). A `task` page opens with the request a person hands to an agent and carries a `prompt` block; a `concept` page explains one thing and carries none. Closed because the style law names exactly two skeletons: a third genre is a change to how the manual is written, not a value a page may invent.

For whom a page is written (PROP-043 `##AUDIENCE-VALUES`, widened with `agent` by PROP-057 `##OBS-AUDIENCE-AGENT`). The single home of this vocabulary is PROP-043 and its one implementation is `progress_core::model::Audience`; the list is spelled here because `vibe-wire` carries no edge to that crate, the same sanctioned duplication the pivot's `when` conditions make for the same reason. Audiences are never declared on the card — they are derived from the page markup (`##CARD-NO-AUDIENCE-DECLARATION`).

One subject this documentation documents, and where it stands for that subject. A `doc` package may document several, and it can be primary for one and community for another — so the status lives per subject and the package's own `status` is the strongest of them.
The subject's `<group>/<name>` coordinate, exactly as `[[documents]]` spells it.

The semver constraint `[[documents]]` puts on the subject's version. A constraint, not a version: the site picks the newest documentation whose constraint admits the subject version a reader is looking at (`##REL-VERSION-SELECTION`).

The documentation this package adapts into its own language (PROP-057 §5), present only in a translation's manifest. It carries neither a revision nor a hash of the source: a «how far behind» comparison needs a history the project does not keep, and the check that exists compares structure against the source as it is now (`##LOC-NO-REVISION`).
The source documentation's `<group>/<name>` coordinate, exactly as `[translates]` spells it.
The semver constraint `[translates]` puts on the source documentation's version.

The documentation's card, its language and its officiality — the arXiv-style row of PROP-057 `##CARD-DECISION`: a title a person reads, the publisher beside it, the abstract that says what the thing covers and for whom.

Who published this documentation — the package's group, printed beside the title wherever the title appears (`##DISC-PUBLISHER-VISIBLE`). Named as its own member rather than left to be re-derived from `group`, because the shell parses nothing and computes nothing (`##PIPE-SHELL-PARSES-NOTHING`): every value it shows arrives named.

The display name on shelves, in the selector, in the page heading and in the catalogue (`##CARD-TITLE`). Required for kind `doc`; identity stays the coordinate, so two documentations may share a title.
What it covers, for whom, what it assumes known, what it leaves out — three to six sentences in the package's own language, bounded at about a thousand characters (`##CARD-DESCRIPTION-AND-ABSTRACT`).

The language every page in this manifest is written in — the package's `[i18n].canonical`, a BCP-47 tag, `en` when the manifest declares none (`##LOC-LANGUAGE-FIELD`). There is no second `lang` field on a package and no list of languages here: another language is another package, found through its `translates` edge.

The strongest standing this documentation holds over any of its subjects — the one value a shelf, a star and a catalogue row need when a package documents more than one thing. The per-subject truth is in `subjects`.

Every subject of `[[documents]]`, which a `doc` package is required to declare at least one of (`##REL-DOCUMENTS-REQUIRED`). Emitted even when empty: a manifest built over a manifest that broke that rule must show the emptiness, not hide it.
Every audience any page of this documentation is written for, sorted and without repetition — the audiences a catalogue row shows. Derived from the page markup, never declared.
The one-line subtitle for lists and the page's meta description; absent when the package declares none.
Present exactly when this package is a translation — that is, when it declares `[translates]`. Its absence is what says «this is a source documentation», so no second flag exists to disagree with it.
One page: where it is, what it is, who it is for, what it says first, and how long it takes to read.

The page's address inside the package — a `/`-separated path under the package's spec root, `model/lock-and-store.xml`. Forward slashes on every platform, so one manifest reads the same everywhere, and the site's address map turns it into a URL without an index (`##SITE-MOUNT`).
The page's H1.
Who the page is written for, sorted and without repetition, from the `audience` of its `<status>` markers. Empty means the page marked none, which the coverage gate can see and a guess would hide.

Every named anchor the page carries, in document order: the title's id, each section's id, each fact's id. These are the immutable addresses a citation may point at (`##INV-ANCHORS-IMMUTABLE`); the positional `pNN` numbers are NOT here, because they live by the current text and would turn a manifest into a promise the next edit breaks.

The page's leading fact — its first paragraph, which the style law requires to stand alone and names as the page's line in `llms.txt` (`AUTHORING.md` §7). Taken, never composed: a summary written by the pipeline would be a second description of the page that nobody proofreads.
